item.text: {"text":"Sampled softmax is compatible with NextItNet’s causal convolutional backbone: the original paper explicitly proposes it as an alternative to full-catalog softmax ([NextItNet](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf)). A 2024 analysis shows that sampled softmax already emphasizes high-scoring negatives through its gradients; temperature controls that emphasis, with excessively low temperatures allowing a few difficult negatives to dominate ([Wu et al., 2024](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf)). Thus, increasing negative count and tuning temperature provide a useful baseline before adding explicit mining. Scalable Cross-Entropy similarly targets informative catalog outputs using approximate maximum-inner-product search, although its efficiency and accuracy findings do not establish gains for this Electronics benchmark ([SCE, 2024](https://dspace.mit.edu/entities/publication/5392aca9-0bae-4176-9b3a-a8165957ba26)).\n\nHardness alone is unreliable evidence of negative relevance. UFNRec documents false negatives in sequential recommendation, but its teacher-based correction should not be imported into this single-model experiment ([UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116)). A 2026 contrastive-recommendation study uses a controlled hard/random mixture and filters both overly similar and overly distant candidates ([EMM](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0893608026004090)). Practical hypothesis, rather than an established NextItNet result: compare uniform sampled softmax against a modest mixture of random and moderately hard negatives scored by the same network; exclude padding, targets, and known training positives, and soften or discard extreme candidates rather than asserting they are true negatives. Keep inference unchanged and select by pinned macro validation HR@10 across all four categories. Lower training loss or larger positive–negative margins cannot establish ranking generalization."}
